name: testimonial-guide
title: How to film a patient testimonial
setup: Phone on a tripod, at eye level
Window light on the patient's face
Patient talks to you, not the lens

prompts.references: Reference images in src/assets/images/testimonial/: ref-portrait.jpg (the patient's face), ref-clinic.jpg (the clinic background), and character.jpg once generated from the character prompt.
prompts.character: Use the attached portrait as the identity reference: keep her face, features, skin tone, eye colour and hairstyle exactly. Photorealistic character reference sheet of an elegant, approachable white woman in her early-to-mid 30s, three views side by side on a plain warm light-grey studio background: (1) front head-and-shoulders, (2) three-quarter view from the waist up, (3) seated in a modern armchair, legs crossed, hands relaxed in her lap. Wardrobe: a fitted black fine-gauge merino mock-neck sweater with a subtle vertical rib knit, sleeves pushed just above the wrist, ribbed cuffs and hem; tailored high-waisted black wide-leg trousers; pointed black leather flats. Jewellery: small gold huggie hoop earrings, one thin gold chain necklace worn over the knit, a slim gold watch. Fresh, natural makeup: even dewy skin, soft brown eyeliner, groomed brows, neutral rose lip. Soft, even studio light that keeps texture in the black knit. 85mm, f/4, natural skin texture, no text, no watermark.
prompts.still: Image 1 is the character reference: keep her face, hair, black rib-knit mock-neck sweater and gold jewellery identical. Image 2 is the clinic background: keep this room, its furniture, colours and lighting. She sits in a modern upholstered armchair placed 2 to 3 metres in front of the background, so the clinic falls softly out of focus behind her. Soft key light from a large window camera-left, gentle fill from the right, subtle warm rim light separating the black sweater from the background. Photorealistic vertical 9:16 video still, natural skin texture, clean modern cinematic grade. She talks to an off-camera interviewer standing just beside the lens, never into the lens. No text, no watermark. Shot:

clips.tip: Head in the top third, a little space above
clips.question: Tell us a little about yourself. What brought you in?
clips.prompt: Medium shot from the waist up, 50mm at f/2, camera at her eye level 30 degrees to her right. Her head sits in the upper third with a little headroom. Hands resting in her lap, a warm, slightly shy smile as she starts to answer.

clips.angle: 45° to the other side · eye level
clips.tip: Shoulders up for the emotional moments
clips.question: What was bothering you before treatment?
clips.prompt: Close-up from the top of the shoulders up, 85mm at f/2, camera at eye level 45 degrees to her left. Thoughtful, slightly vulnerable expression, eyes lowered for a moment as she remembers.

clips.angle: Straight on · slightly off the lens
clips.tip: Show the clinic, keep the background tidy
clips.question: What made you decide to finally do something about it?
clips.prompt: Medium-wide shot showing her from the knees up in the armchair with the clinic clearly readable behind her, 35mm at f/2.8, camera almost straight on at eye level. Sitting upright, determined, speaking.

clips.tip: Frame past your shoulder for a conversation feel
clips.question: How did our team make you feel during treatment?
clips.prompt: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind an interviewer whose out-of-focus shoulder and back of head fill the left third of the frame, 50mm at f/2. She faces the interviewer, listening, gentle smile.

clips.tip: Eyes and smile in frame, hold steady
clips.question: How do you feel when you smile now?
clips.prompt: Extreme close-up from eyebrows to chin, 85mm at f/2, eye level, slightly off-axis to her right. A soft, closed-lip smile building.

clips.tip: End wide and let them finish the thought
clips.question: What would you tell someone who's still on the fence?
clips.prompt: Wide shot of the clinic room with her seated full-length in the armchair in the middle third, 24mm at f/4, eye level. Leaning forward slightly, speaking with conviction.

cta: Send us your clips. We'll handle the edit.
